papers.what_it_is: A preprint that trains shallow parametrised quantum circuits, simulated on classical hardware, to act as POVMs that discriminate non-orthogonal quantum states, with a cost function that trades error against inconclusive outcomes.

existing.note: The statement holds for the test with training data centred at a0 (the unambiguous-discrimination comparison with a prior optical experiment), not for all training. It is in Section 3 (p.7, Fig. 3 on p.8), not Section 4. The paper adds that a close-to-minimum Pinc is reachable if a small non-zero error probability is allowed, and attributes part of the gap to the training data being centred at, not fixed at, a0.
existing.value: The authors report that, in repeated experiments with training data centred at a0, training did not on average reach the theoretical minimum inconclusiveness Pinc when a high penalty forced the error probability Perr close to zero, and that allowing a small non-zero error probability gave a Pinc close to the theoretical minimum, so a less strict constraint on Perr allows a much lower inconclusiveness rate. The experiment uses exact measurement probabilities on a simulated quantum computer.

existing.note: The abstract says 'comparable performance to theoretically optimal POVMs'. The body gives two reference points in Fig. 2: at a0 = 0.25 the success probability is 0.84 against a stated optimum of 0.833; at a0 = 0.50 it is 0.59 against a stated optimum of 0.666. papers.what_it_is: A preprint that builds an LSTM cell from six variational quantum circuits (QLSTM) and compares it in noiseless simulation with a 166-parameter classical LSTM on five time-series tasks, including sine, a damped pendulum, a Bessel function and two open-quantum-system dynamics.
